knowledge_answers.rationale: Bowled applies when the delivered ball puts the wicket down, even after first touching bat or person.
Wide does not bar Stumped; when the keeper-only, out-of-ground and no-run conditions hold, Stumped applies even if Run out might otherwise appear justified.
An umpire may alter a decision when the alteration is made promptly; the prompt-correction power does not make decisions indefinitely revisable.

Using a deliberately discarded object is illegal fielding; the ball becomes dead and completed plus already-crossed running is retained; five Penalty runs go to the batting side and the delivery does not count in the over.

A striker with a runner has special ground rules at the keeper's end; when the striker is out of ground both Run out and Stumped might initially appear; if the runner is also out there, Law 25.6.5 restricts the outcome to Run out only.
